# fix(hfp-008): deleting a Project fails once a Participant has Segments

## Task

Deleting a User or a Project fails with a foreign key error as soon as one of its Participants has Segments. The delete cascades to `participants`, but `segments_participant_id_project_id_fkey` is `NO ACTION`. Postgres checks it before the cascade through `transcripts` has removed the segments. This bug was already there before HFP-006.

ADR 0004 says this case is "resolved within the same delete". That isn't true today. Once transcript upload exists, deleting a real Project in the UI (HFP-007) will return a 500.

Likely fix: make that foreign key `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED`, so it is checked at commit, after the cascade has finished. Deleting a single Participant on its own is still blocked, as ADR 0004 intends.

## Parent Story

Hosted-first pivot (ADR 0001), data model (ADR 0004). Found in HFP-006 (#26).

## Blocked by

Nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A migration (written by the owner) makes `segments (participant_id, project_id) → participants (id, project_id)` deferrable and initially deferred. The down section restores `NO ACTION`, not deferrable.
- [ ] Server test: deleting a Project with a transcript, a Participant and a spoken Segment succeeds and removes all of them.
- [ ] Server test: deleting a Participant who still has Segments is still rejected.
- [ ] Deleting a User with such a Project also succeeds. Covered by a test, or checked by hand and noted in `progress.md`.
- [ ] `dbmate rollback` + `dbmate up` run cleanly. `db/schema.sql` is updated and `npm run db:test:prepare` is re-run.
- [ ] ADR 0004's delete paragraph says how the exception is resolved (deferred check).

## Suggested label

`ready-for-human` (the owner writes migrations by hand)
